# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v2 c1 P48](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0048), [v2 c26 P15](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0015)</sub>
- **Role:** Housewife and church/community worker  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v2 c14 P5](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an elderly, active woman who keeps a constant watch over Avonlea from her kitchen window. In her later years, her hands are work-hardened from a life of constant labor.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P45](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0045), [v2 c26 P1](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0001)_

## Personality

Mrs. Lynde is a capable, energetic, and outspoken woman who prides herself on always speaking her mind without fear or favor. She is deeply busy, highly inquisitive, and possesses a sharp eye for her neighbors' affairs, earning a reputation as a meddlesome gossip. Despite her critical, blunt manner and nagging tendencies, she is a kind-hearted, charitable, and dependable neighbor who works tirelessly for her church and community. She is also capable of owning up to her mistakes when proven wrong.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c1 P30](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0030), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P45](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0045), [v1 c10 P1](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0001), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c31 P4](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0004), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the Avonlea main road, where she kept close watch over everything passing by while running local church societies and knitting quilts. When Matthew Cuthbert brought orphan Anne Shirley to Green Gables, Rachel was astonished and visited to inspect her; her blunt criticism of Anne's freckles and red hair sparked a fiery temper outburst from the girl. After Anne delivered a dramatic apology, Rachel forgave her, allowed her to pick lilies in her garden, and gradually grew to admire her progress and beauty over the years. Following a severe illness with the grippe, Rachel continued her energetic community work, including heading church bazaars, political rallies, and advising Marilla Cuthbert on raising children. When her meek husband Thomas fell ill and passed away, Rachel was forced to sell their mortgaged farm. Rather than move out West with her children or live with her daughter Eliza, she accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables to live together. She continued supervising household life at Green Gables, helping care for the adopted twins Davy and Dora Keith, and attending church events despite occasional accidents like twisting her ankle or falling down cellar stairs. Years later, she happily helped prepare for Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe at Green Gables, bringing homemade gifts and plum pudding to visit Anne and Gilbert in Four Winds for Christmas.
